description: HIGH-SPEED MULTI-ACTION PIPELINE: Executes 2 or more sequential browser actions in a single round-trip without waiting for LLM turns between steps. PREFER THIS over individual single-action calls (e.g. typing + pressing Enter, filling multiple form fields, clicking tabs/buttons then waiting, searching, navigating + reading) to drastically slash latency and token burn. Supports native primitives (browser_click, browser_fill, browser_type, browser_type_secret, browser_navigate, browser_key, browser_scroll, browser_wait, browser_map, etc.) plus ergonomic macro steps (type_and_send, click_and_wait, navigate_and_read, scroll_and_read, fill_form). If compile_from_history: true is passed, automatically compiles recent successful session trail actions into a burst macro.

app.description: Electron app name configured in config.json under 'electron'.

batch.description: If true, defers action map generation until all steps are complete to maximize throughput.

compile_from_history.description: Compile recent successful session trail actions into a macro. If steps are omitted, executes the compiled macro directly.

dry_run.description: If true with compile_from_history, returns the compiled steps without executing them.

history_limit.description: Number of recent session trail entries to consider when compile_from_history is true (default: 20).

steps.description: Ordered array of tool calls or macros to execute serially. Either 'steps' or 'actions' may be passed.

args.description: Tool arguments. Alternatively, arguments may be specified flat on the step object.

tool.description: Tool name or macro step (e.g. browser_click, browser_fill, browser_type, type_and_send, click_and_wait, navigate_and_read, scroll_and_read, fill_form).

stop_on_error.description: Halt execution immediately if a step fails to prevent cascading failures (default: true).

name: browser_burst
